Exxon signs shale deal with Azerbaijan for Middle Kura Basin
article:
(Sept 26): ExxonMobil Holdings Corp agreed to pump oil and natural gas from Azerbaijan’s shale fields as the Texas energy giant takes its fracking expertise overseas.

ExxonMobil has entered a joint venture with Azerbaijan’s state oil company Socar that will allow it to explore and develop “unconventional hydrocarbon resources” in the Middle Kura Basin, the companies said in a statement. ExxonMobil will operate the project, pending approval by the country’s legislature.

US shale has been the largest source of new global oil supplies for the past 15 years, transforming the country into the biggest producer of crude and exporter of liquefied natural gas. ExxonMobil and others are keen to take the lessons learned in the Permian Basin and other US shale fields to countries with similar geologic endowments.

The legal and regulatory structures governing such drilling and oil production often are more complicated than in the US, requiring extensive negotiations before operations commence. ExxonMobil and Socar have been in talks for more than a year on the commercial and other aspects of the deal, which has been encouraged by the Trump administration.

“We will combine Socar’s knowledge of Azerbaijan with ExxonMobil’s global experience and technology to better understand the basin’s potential and pursue opportunities for safe and efficient development,” said Bart Cahir, an ExxonMobil senior vice-president.

title: South Korea tax windfall seen above 50 tril won — Yonhap
article:
(Sept 27): South Korea’s excess tax revenue may exceed 50 trillion won (US$37 billion) this year, according to a Yonhap News report, reflecting factors including a stronger-than-expected semiconductor cycle.

That could push the size of the Future Response Fund, a government tool that channels excess tax revenue into strategic investments and fiscal reserves, to above 200 trillion won, according to Yonhap’s calculations.

The Ministry of Economy and Finance is expected to publish the figure in its revised 2026 national tax revenue estimate due later this month, according to the report.

The revenue windfall would give the government more room to increase spending without a corresponding rise in borrowing. Under the 2027 budget proposal, much of the semiconductor-driven windfall is set to flow towards helping finance AI, chips and youth support, while limiting bond issuance and building a fiscal buffer.

The finance ministry said in a statement on Sunday that no decision has been finalised on the revised estimate of this year’s national tax revenue.
